class.name: Spellsword
class.tagline: A swordsman who writes spells into the edge of the blade.
class.fantasy: Spellswords learned their letters in the hedge-mages' towers and then picked up a sword. They inscribe sigils along the blade before a fight, so every cut carries fire, frost or storm, and when enough of that power has built up in the steel they release it all at once. Woven differently, the same sigils become wards that turn blows aside, and a Spellsword in that form holds the front of a fight like any shield-bearer.
class.role_text: Two forms make two roles from one kit. In Wardweave Form the Spellsword wears its Intellect as armor, builds threat with every spell and soaks damage in runic wards. In Bladesong Form the same Edges and Releases hit hard instead. The third tree, Arcana, leans further into spells for a damage dealer who fights at sword's length and a little beyond.
class.stats: Strength and Intellect, with Stamina for tanking. Attack power from Strength as a Man-at-Arms; a quarter of attack power adds to the damage of Edges and Releases (Bladecraft); in Wardweave Form each point of Intellect is worth 2 armor.
compare: The other tank and melee fighter. A Man-at-Arms runs on rage and plate; a Spellsword runs on mana, wears mail at most and turns Intellect into armor and wards.
Also mixes weapon and spell, but heals and buffs the party. The Spellsword has no heals: its magic goes into the blade and its own wards.
Also an arcane, fire and frost caster, from range in cloth. The Spellsword casts mostly through the sword, at melee range or a few yards off.

mechanics.name: Edges
mechanics.summary: A sigil on the blade: one at a time.
text: An Edge is inscribed on your weapon for 60 minutes (instant, off the global cooldown). Your melee hits then deal extra damage of its school and carry its effect: Flame Edge burns, Frost Edge chills, Storm Edge arcs to another enemy, Warding Edge gives you a small absorb shield.
The Edge also decides what Release does.

mechanics.name: Resonance
mechanics.summary: Power built up in the steel, 0 to 5.
text: Each melee hit while you have an Edge gives 1 Resonance (2 on a critical strike), up to 5. It fades 10 seconds after combat.
Release spends all of it, for an effect per point that depends on your Edge. Hold it for 5 or spend it early: the choice is the class's rhythm.

mechanics.name: Release
text: Flame Edge: Flame Burst, fire damage to every enemy within 8 yards.
Frost Edge: Rime Lance, frost damage to one enemy up to 20 yards away, rooting it for 1 second per Resonance.
Storm Edge: Thunderclap, nature damage to the target and up to 3 enemies near it, interrupting their spells.
Warding Edge: Bulwark of Runes, an absorb shield on you per Resonance, and high threat on every enemy within 10 yards.

mechanics.name: Forms
mechanics.summary: Bladesong for damage, Wardweave for tanking.
text: Bladesong Form: you deal 10% more damage and your critical strikes give an extra Resonance.
Wardweave Form: each point of Intellect gives 2 armor, you cause 45% more threat, take 10% less damage and deal 10% less, and your absorb shields are 20% stronger.
Changing form costs no mana and keeps your Resonance, but has a 1.5 second cooldown.

mechanics.name: Bladecraft
text: A quarter of your attack power is added to the damage of your Edges and Releases, so the same Strength-and-Intellect gear serves both halves of the class.

builds.name: Warden
builds.text: The tank: Wardweave Form, Warding Edge, Reprisal off parries, Aegis of Runes and Bastion of Glyphs for big pulls, with Arcana for cheaper spells and longer reach.

builds.name: Bladedancer
builds.text: Melee damage: Bladesong Form with Twin Edge (Flame and Storm), Sigil Flurry for Resonance and Thousand Cuts for packs.

builds.name: Arcblade
builds.text: Spell damage at a few yards: Arcane Lance and Overload for burst, Release from range with Frost Edge, Arc of Ruin to finish.

bots: Takes Wardweave Form and Warding Edge when it's the party's tank (the only member with a shield, or when told), Bladesong Form with Flame or Storm Edge otherwise.

Tanking: Hurl Blade to pull, Reprisal whenever it can, Release at 3 Resonance or more for threat and a shield, Mark of Challenge on anything attacking someone else, Challenging Glyph when three or more are loose, Last Sigil below 30% health.
Damage: Arcane Strike on cooldown, Release at 5 Resonance (Flame Burst when crowded, Thunderclap on casters), Arc Cleave against several enemies, Arcane Surge on elites and bosses.
Interrupts casting creatures with Severing Sigil, as other bots do with Hilt Strike and Hush.
Party bar buff categories: Edge (Auto, Flame, Frost, Storm, Warding) and Form (Auto, Bladesong, Wardweave).
implementation: A class id of our own in ClassicData (classic's nine are taken), a trainer list, race pairings and talent data from our own files, as for any new class.

Every ability is new, in our own spell file. Most map to classic effect and aura types: Edges are weapon imbues like classic's Rockbiter and Flametongue, Runic Ward an absorb, Mark of Challenge a taunt, Severing Sigil an interrupt, Phase Step a blink to the target, Binding Glyph a trap.
A second resource beside mana, kept on the Combatant like combo points but on the caster, with a counter on the player frame. Release reads the active Edge to pick its effect.
Two shapeshift auras on the stance bar, as Man-at-Arms stances are. Wardweave's armor from Intellect and threat multiplier are stat and threat auras CharacterStats and Enemy already read.
Our talent rules cover the trees; Twin Edge needs two imbues at once, the one new piece.
Bot logic for both roles, choosing the role by the party, and the Edge and Form categories on the party bar.
No new item types: swords, mail and shields with Strength, Intellect and Stamina exist. The game would want a few more Strength-and-Intellect pieces at low levels.
